chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad together, from Ibn Mahboub, from Khalid ibn Jarir, from Abu Al-Rabie, who said:

Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who lent a man dirhams, so he returned to him better ones from them with his own goodwill, and the borrower and the lender knew that he had only lent them so that better ones would be given back from them. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem when the borrower agreed himself.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to return better quality coins when repaying a loan of money in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that voluntary enhancement of the principal in a qard (interest-free loan) is permissible, distinguishing it from riba by emphasizing the borrower's free will rather than a contractual obligation. This ruling highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding financial transactions, allowing for goodwill gestures even when the intention was known from the outset. The hadith underscores the importance of consent and lack of compulsion in validating such financial exchanges.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, and Ahmad Bin Muhammad altogether, from Ibn Mahboub, from Khalid Bin Jareer, from Abu Al Rabie who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> was asked about a man who lent Dirhams to a man, so he returned to him good ones from it with agreement from himself, and the borrower and the lender knew that rather it was lent in order for good ones to be given back from it’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem when the borrower agreed himself’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad all from ibn Mahbub from Khalid ibn Jarir from abu al-Rabi‘ who has said the following: “

Once abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was asked about the case of a man who gave a loan to another man who paid it back with better dirhams without compulsion, and the creditor knew it as well as the debtor that the loan was given to receive payment with the better dirhams. He (the Imam) said, Tt is not unlawful.’”
